topics.description: A landlocked country in the African Great Lakes region, associated with Hutu, Tutsi, and Batwa populations and the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These conflicts have been referred to as the “African World Wars” with at least nine countries participating in its second of them. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this set of conflicts. Mobutu Sese Seko was ousted in the first of these conflicts, while his rival Laurent Kabila was killed during the second.
parts.answer: Congo Wars [or Congo Crises; or Congolese Civil Wars; accept First and Second Congo Wars]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] The Congo Wars were catalyzed in part by this ethnic group, which fled to the DRC from a neighboring country to escape Hutu persecution.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This country’s namesake genocide against its Tutsi population was ended by its president Paul Kagame, who led this country to invade the DRC during the Congo Wars.
parts.answer: Rwanda [or Republic of Rwanda or Republika y’u Rwanda]

topics.description: The British Olympic-class ocean liner that sank after striking an iceberg in the North Atlantic on April 15, 1912, during its maiden voyage.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Chaplain and photographer Francis Browne documented this ship’s stops at Cherbourg and Queenstown after it initially departed from Southampton. Architect Thomas Andrews diagnosed the (*) “mathematical certainty” that awaited this ship on the morning of April 15th once six of its compartments had flooded. Edward Smith died while captaining, for ten points, what “unsinkable” ocean liner that, in 1912, sank after striking an iceberg?

parts.label: L
parts.question: In 1912, the Royal Albert Hall hosted an enormous benefit concert for the families of the musicians who played during a maritime tragedy. Answer the following about the concert, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: The concert memorialized the band of this “unsinkable” White Star Line ship, which sank while sailing from England to America in 1912.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The concert included a performance of this composer’s Funeral March. This Polish composer also wrote the Revolutionary Etude ´ and the Minute Waltz.
parts.answer: Fred´ eric ´ Chopin (accept Fred´ eric Franc¸ois ´ Chopin; accept Fryderyk Franciszek Chopin)

parts.label: C
parts.question: This British composer conducted part of the concert, which included a performance of this man’s Enigma Variations.
parts.answer: Edward Elgar (accept Sir Edward William Elgar)

topics.description: The 1979 revolution that overthrew Iran’s Pahlavi monarchy and established the Islamic Republic under Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country was ruled by the Qajar (kuh-jer) Dynasty, which was overthrown in the White Revolution. After this country's eponymous revolution, the failed Operation Eagle Claw attempted to free 66 American diplomatic hostages. Those hostages were held for 444 days after an attack on the US (*) embassy from students under Ayatollah Khomeini. For ten points, name this country led by Hassan Rhouani from Tehran.
parts.answer: Iran [or the Islamic Republic of Iran]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An instigating factor for this event was the death of over sixty people in Jaleh (JAH-leh) Square  on “Black Friday.” This event ultimately brought to power a man who advocated the  Guardianship of the Jurist system. During this event, the SAVAK (SAH-vahk) secret police were  dissolved and a man whose ideas were popularized on clandestine (*) cassette tapes returned from  exile in Najaf (nah-JAHF). Student supporters of this event stormed an American embassy and took 66  hostages. The Pahlavi (PAH-lah-vee) Dynasty ended in, for 10 points, what 1979 event that brought  Ayatollah Khomeini (AI-uh-toh-lah koh-may-NEE) to power?
parts.answer: Iranian Revolution of 1979 [or Islamic Revolution; or Enqelāb-e Eslāmī]

topics.description: The network of detention, forced-labor, concentration, and extermination camps established and operated by Nazi Germany and its collaborators during the Holocaust and World War II.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Note to players: description acceptable. Juliek (YOO-lee-eck) and Moshe the Beadle appear in a novel that takes place in these locations. An author who died in one of these locations wrote the line "In spite of everything I still believe that people are really good at heart" in the (*) diary she kept in Amsterdam. Elie Wiesel's Night is set in and Anne Frank died in one of, for 10 points, what places which included Auschwitz (ow-shvitz)?
parts.answer: concentration camps [accept anything indicating [Nazi] death camps or other obvious equivalents]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Primo Levi describes working in one of these places as a chemist in his short story “Cerium.” In one  book, the narrator declares God “is hanging here from this gallows” after seeing an execution in one of these  places. In that memoir, the villagers of (*) Sighet ignore the warnings of Moishe the Beadle and are deported to  one of these places. For 10 points, Elie Wiesel’s Night is primarily set in what type of location, where Jews were  sent during the Holocaust?
parts.answer: concentration camps [or death camps; or extermination camps; accept specific locations, such as  Auschwitz]

topics.description: The 1979–1981 diplomatic crisis in which Iranian militants held American embassy personnel hostage in Tehran for 444 days.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country was ruled by the Qajar (kuh-jer) Dynasty, which was overthrown in the White Revolution. After this country's eponymous revolution, the failed Operation Eagle Claw attempted to free 66 American diplomatic hostages. Those hostages were held for 444 days after an attack on the US (*) embassy from students under Ayatollah Khomeini. For ten points, name this country led by Hassan Rhouani from Tehran.
parts.answer: Iran [or the Islamic Republic of Iran]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In 1998, al-Qaeda bombed two U.S. examples of these buildings in Nairobi and Dar-Es Salaam. After a revolution brought Ayatollah Khomeni to power, militant students seized one of these buildings in Tehran, causing a (*) “hostage crisis” that lasted 444 days. Country capitals are home to many “foreign” examples of, for 10 points, what kind of buildings, the workplace of diplomats and ambassadors?

topics.description: The people and national community associated with France.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A “citizen” of this ethnicity was recalled by The Mountain for violating George Washington’s Neutrality Proclamation. Agents of this ethnicity demanded bribes from Pinckney, Marshall, and Gerry to see a minister during the (*) XYZ Affair. This ethnicity’s “Hero of Two Worlds” captured Redoubt 9 during the Battle of Yorktown. For 10 points, name this ethnicity of Minister Talleyrand and Gilbert du Motier, the Marquis de Lafayette.

topics.description: Russian politician who has served as president or prime minister of Russia since 1999 and is a former KGB officer.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Protesters in this leader's country's chanted for this man to "have some tea" after this leader was accused of having the tea of his political opponent Alexei Navalny poisoned. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this world leader, who recently gained the power to potentially stay in office until 2036 after his country voted for constitutional changes that extended term limits.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] For years, Vladimir Putin has served as the president of this largest nation in the world by area.
parts.answer: Russia [or the Russian Federation; accept Rossiya]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Amid August 2020 protests in this country, Putin gave military support to this country's leader Alexander Lukashenko, who is often called "Europe's last dictator."

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In 2019, this politician was beat by Mostik, an orange tabby cat, to be the first to cross the Kerch Strait Bridge. In 2021, this politician approved a change to his country’s (*) constitution that allows him to extend his presidency, which has bounced back and forth between this man and Dmitry Medvedev since 1999. For ten points, name this frequently-shirtless ex-KGB agent who is the president of Russia.

topics.description: The minted currency of ancient Rome and the Roman world, including denominations such as the denarius, sestertius, follis, and solidus, used for commerce and imperial representation.

parts.label: L
parts.question: It is said that Rome tilled the ground around Carthage with this resource, so the city would never thrive again. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this resource. The word “salary” comes from money paid to Roman soldiers to buy this resource, which was valuable for its ability to preserve and flavor food.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Romans adopted the use of this other kind of currency from the Greeks. Early Roman forms of these things included the Sestertius and Follis, which were often minted with the current Emperor’s head on one side.

parts.label: C
parts.question: Roman coins lost value during the Crisis of the Third Century due to this economic phenomenon. Emperor Diocletian minted a new coin, the Solidus, to counteract this phenomenon.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about damnatio memoriae, or the literal erasure of public figures in ancient Rome. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Erasing the memories of people sometimes meant re-arranging homes to disrupt the technique of “memory palaces” illustrated by this man in De Oratore. Mark Antony’s wife Fulvia stabbed the tongue of this master orator.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Erasing the images of governors or emperors was often difficult because they appeared on these objects like the denarius or libra. These objects were commonly minted in silver and used to purchase in Roman forums.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] After burying the Vestal Virgin Cornelia alive amongst other cruel acts, this dynasty’s last member Domitian was subject to a damnatio memoriae. This dynasty arose under Vespasian after the Year of the Four Emperors.

topics.description: The 1962 Cold War confrontation over the Soviet deployment of nuclear missiles to Cuba, which brought the United States and Soviet Union close to nuclear war.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man's 1957 visit to the Turkish embassy in his country ended a summer crisis over military  influence in Syria. This leader, who launched the failed Virgin Lands Campaign, left the Four  Powers Summit after only a day due to tensions over the (*) U-2 incident. The satellite Sputnik was  launched under this leader, with whom Fidel Castro struck a deal to place nuclear missiles in Cuba. This  leader's “Secret Speech” denounced the repression of the Stalin era. For 10 points, name this Soviet  politician who bested Georgy Malenkov in a 1950s leadership struggle.

topics.description: The 1970 Canadian political crisis caused by Front de libération du Québec kidnappings and the federal government’s invocation of the War Measures Act.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This prime minister proposed sharing oil revenues in the National Energy Program, leading to  a national debate on “western alienation.” This prime minister outlined his urban reform and  minority improvement plans called a “Just Society.” After the death of Pierre Laporte, this man  told reporters (*) “just watch me” following his invocation of the War Measures Act during the  October Crisis. Support for this politician inspired a namesake “mania” in a 1968 election. For 10 points,  name this Liberal Canadian prime minister during the 1970s.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Pierre Trudeau [Pierre Yves Elliott Trudeau; prompt on Trudeau]

parts.label: L
parts.question: This province's sovereignty movement grew stronger during its “Quiet Revolution.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this largest Canadian province, the only majority French-speaking one.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Under Pierre, a prime minister from this family, Quebec separatists caused a crisis by kidnapping two government officials. The current Canadian Prime Minister, Justin, is from this family.
parts.answer: Trudeau [accept Pierre Trudeau or Justin Trudeau]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] The kidnappings caused a crisis named for this month. It's not November, but, in another country, a revolution named for this month ended the provisional government of Alexander Kerensky.
parts.answer: October [accept October Crisis or October Revolution]
